Adventure Bikes: The UK Touring Favourite

Adventure bikes dominate UK touring for good reason. Their upright riding position, long-travel suspension, and versatile nature handle everything from motorway miles to green lane exploration. But with over a dozen models competing in the category, choosing the right one requires careful comparison.

How We Compare

We evaluate adventure bikes across five key touring criteria: comfort on long rides, weather protection, luggage capability, off-road ability, and value for money. Each bike is scored on real-world touring use rather than paper specifications.

The Top 10 Adventure Bikes 2026

1. BMW R 1300 GS — The benchmark. New telelever front end, 143bhp boxer, and the most comprehensive electronics package available. Expensive but nothing else offers this breadth of capability. Score: 95/100.

2. Triumph Tiger 1200 Rally Pro — The best engine in the class. The 1160cc triple delivers character and performance in equal measure. Shaft drive and semi-active suspension seal the deal. Score: 93/100.

3. KTM 1390 Super Adventure S — The sportiest adventure bike with a 1350cc V-twin producing 173bhp. Incredible electronics and suspension but the aggressive character divides opinion. Score: 90/100.

4. Honda Africa Twin CRF1100L — The most capable off-road machine in the big adventure class. DCT option removes clutch fatigue. Honda reliability is legendary. Score: 89/100.

5. Yamaha Tenere 700 — The lightweight rebel. At 204kg and with a brilliant CP2 engine, it proves you do not need 1200cc and electronics to have adventures. Arguably the most fun on B-roads. Score: 88/100.

6. Ducati DesertX Rally — Italian flair with genuine off-road DNA. The Testastretta engine is characterful, the chassis is sharp, and the styling is stunning. Less practical than rivals but more exciting. Score: 86/100.

7. Kawasaki Versys 1000 SE — The underrated tourer. Incredibly smooth inline four, electronic suspension, and outstanding comfort. Less capable off-road but superb on tarmac. Score: 85/100.

8. Suzuki V-Strom 1050DE — Improved off-road credentials with wire wheels and longer suspension travel. The V-twin is smooth and reliable. Excellent value. Score: 84/100.

9. Aprilia Tuareg 660 — Middleweight adventure with a 659cc twin. Light, agile, and genuinely capable off-road. The most fun middleweight adventure bike available. Score: 83/100.

10. Harley-Davidson Pan America 1250 — Surprising capability from Harley. The Revolution Max engine is strong and the adaptive ride height system aids confidence at stops. Score: 82/100.

Test ride before you buy. Adventure bikes have very different characters — a BMW GS feels nothing like a KTM Super Adventure. Your body shape, riding style, and priorities should guide your choice, not brand loyalty.

Budget Considerations

New adventure bikes range from seven thousand for the Tenere 700 to over twenty thousand for a fully-specced BMW GS. Factor in luggage, protection, and comfort accessories which can add two to four thousand pounds to the purchase price. Read our Best Touring Motorcycles for UK Roads in 2026 guide for more. keyTakeaways: The BMW R 1300 GS tops the ranking at 95/100 for sheer breadth of capability.
The Triumph Tiger 1200 Rally Pro offers the best engine in class with shaft drive.
The Yamaha Tenere 700 proves you do not need 1200cc to have real adventures.
Prices span seven thousand for the Tenere to over twenty thousand for a specced GS.
Test riding matters as a GS feels nothing like a KTM Super Adventure.

faq.q: Which adventure bike is best overall?
faq.a: The BMW R 1300 GS scores highest at 95/100 thanks to its new Telelever front end, 143bhp boxer and the most comprehensive electronics package available. It is expensive, but nothing else offers this breadth of capability across motorways, B-roads and green lanes.

faq.q: Do I need a 1200cc adventure bike?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The Yamaha Tenere 700 scores 88/100 and is arguably the most fun on B-roads at just 204kg with a brilliant CP2 engine. For solo UK touring, a lighter middleweight is often more enjoyable than a heavyweight flagship on tight British roads.

faq.q: How much do accessories add to the price?
faq.a: Luggage, protection and comfort accessories can add two to four thousand pounds to the purchase price. New adventure bikes range from around seven thousand for the Tenere 700 to over twenty thousand for a fully-specced BMW GS, so factor kit into your total budget.

faq.q: Is the KTM 1390 too aggressive for touring?
faq.a: The KTM 1390 Super Adventure S is the sportiest option with 173bhp and sharp throttle response, which divides opinion. It scores 90/100 and is superb for riders who enjoy pushing the pace, but the firmer character and higher wind noise make it less relaxing than a GS on long days.
